text: unit cost model mixed effects model country, facility visit type effects covariate effects assumed shared across countries, facilities visit types. Log costs assumed vary normally: log⁡(USD_unitcost_totali)∼N(μi,σ2) \log(\text{USD\_unitcost\_total}_i) \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu_i, \sigma^2) μi\mu_i given : μi=α+∑j=1Jβjxji+γci+δfi+ζvi \mu_i = \alpha + \sum_{j=1}^J{\beta_j x_{ji}} + \gamma_{c_i} +  \delta_{f_i} +  \zeta_{v_i} xjix_{ji} represents value jth covariate, cic_i country, fif_i facility, viv_i visit type observation ii. variables γci\gamma_{c_i}, δfi\delta_{f_i} ζvi\zeta_{v_i} account systematic differences across countries, facilities visit types, respectively, assumed vary normally zero: γc∼N(0,σc2) \gamma_{c} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, \sigma_c^2) δf∼N(0,σf2) \delta_{f} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, \sigma_f^2) ζo∼N(0,σv2) \zeta_{o} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, \sigma_v^2) Model instances created via unitcost function: prior distribution model parameter can visualised calling plot(priors, parameter = "name_of_param"):  posterior (fitted) distribution parameter can generated calling model$plot_posteriors: Figure 1: Fitted beta cefficients Figure 2: Fitted intercept standard deviations random effects

Including output-level random effects in model.  # See model covariates covariates <- model$covariates() print(covariates) #> [1] "public"       "urban"        "healthcentre" "primary"      "secondary"    #> [6] "tertiary"     "logVisits"  # See priors used in the model priors <- model$priors() print(priors) #> $prior.alpha.mean #> [1] 0 #>  #> $prior.alpha.precision #> [1] 0.01 #>  #> $prior.sigma.scale #> [1] 10 #>  #> $prior.sigma_c.scale #> [1] 0.1 #>  #> $prior.sigma_f.scale #> [1] 10 #>  #> $prior.sigma_v.scale #> [1] 10 #>  #> $prior.beta.mean #> [1] 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 #>  #> $prior.beta.precision #> [1] 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 0.01 #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "capturetbpriors" "list" plots <- list() l <- length(covariates) for(i in 1:l) {   plots[[i]] <- plot(priors, par = paste0("beta[", i, "]")) } plots[[l + 1]] <- plot(priors, par = "alpha") plots[[l + 2]] <- plot(priors, par = "sigma") plots[[l + 3]] <- plot(priors, par = "sigma_c") plots[[l + 4]] <- plot(priors, par = "sigma_f") plots[[l + 5]] <- plot(priors, par = "sigma_v")  do.call(grid.arrange, c(plots, ncol = 3)) #> Warning: Removed 3341 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`). #> Warning: Removed 4926 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`). #> Warning: Removed 3341 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`). #> Removed 3341 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_line()`). model$plot_posteriors(pars = paste0("beta[", 1:length(covariates), "]")) +    scale_y_discrete(labels = covariates) #> Scale for y is already present. #> Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale. model$plot_posteriors(pars = c("alpha", "sigma", "sigma_c", "sigma_f", "sigma_v"))

text: Predictions unit cost new inputs, training set, generated via predict method. code: # Include all covariates plus facility country `fc_country` and visit type `output` new_inputs <- list(   logVisits = 6.9,      n_services = 1,   healthcentre = FALSE,     primary = FALSE,   secondary = FALSE,      tertiary = FALSE,   urban = FALSE,    public = TRUE,   fc_country = "Ethiopia",     output = "op_treatmentvisit" )  # This will center covariates as required by the model prepared_inputs <- capturetb::prepare_covariates(raw = new_inputs, mod = model) pred <- model$predict(prepared_inputs,  scale = "natural",  summarised = TRUE,  centrality = c("mean", "median"),  ci = c(0.95, 0.9, 0.8))  # Expected unit cost is mean prediction expected_unit_cost <- pred$Mean print(expected_unit_cost) #> [1] 13.12743 13.12743 13.12743  knitr::kable(pred) pred <- model$predict(prepared_inputs, scale = "natural", summarised = FALSE) ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(cost = pred), ggplot2::aes(x = cost)) + ggplot2::geom_density()
